clauses.title: Blocking findings are anchored to criteria, clauses, or invariants
clauses.section: ### Finding anchoring and threat-model bound (AC-ANCHOR, CL-D34)
requires: Every `Blocker` or `Major` finding names the acceptance criterion, contract clause, or fail-stop invariant
`reword` finding
owner edit of the body, never an implementation blocker
`follow-up` finding reported with a proposed issue title
the threat model no longer excludes it and the finding is `criterion-anchored` at its own severity
Bounding applies to severity and disposition only
that anchor set replaces the older acceptance-criterion-only test
naming none of the three is an out-of-scope improvement rather than a blocker
that its cited counterexample falsifies or that unavailable required evidence prevents verifying, matching the two finding bases CL-D29 admits

clauses.title: Every Sol payload carries the anchoring bound
clauses.section: #### Sol-only adversarial invariant payload block (AC-ADVERSARIAL-payload, CL-D29)
requires: Every `Blocker` or `Major` finding names the acceptance criterion, contract clause, or fail-stop invariant it falsifies
`reword` finding corrected by owner body edit, not an implementation blocker
`follow-up` finding with a proposed issue title, and is instead `criterion-anchored` at its own severity when a criterion, clause, or invariant names that condition

label every finding that is not an out-of-scope improvement with exactly one of the three anchoring classes `criterion-anchored`, `reword`, or `follow-up`, leaving the pre-existing out-of-scope residual label outside that set (CL-D34)
or that unavailable required evidence prevents verifying, matching the two finding bases CL-D29 admits

clauses.title: Anchoring classes are labelled separately from the closed disposition vocabulary
requires: exactly one anchoring class before its disposition
criterion-anchored
reword
follow-up
disposition `fixed` on the body revision or `accepted-as-designed`
disposition `deferred` with a proposed issue title
every cited counterexample is still reported
keeps the pre-existing out-of-scope label above, which stays outside the three anchoring classes and is unchanged by CL-D34
Label every finding that is not an out-of-scope improvement with exactly one anchoring class
that the cited counterexample falsifies or that unavailable required evidence prevents verifying, covering both finding bases CL-D29 admits

clauses.title: Exact autofix declares its cooperative operator assumptions
requires: assumes these operator conditions cooperative unless an Issue acceptance criterion names one
resolve outside the operator checkout
not mutated by a third party during the run
not concurrently hostile
schema-valid responses for supported endpoints
another writer against the same checkout or workspace
Helpers that detect a violated assumption still fail closed
`follow-up` finding under AC-ANCHOR (CL-D34)
A claim only in PR-body prose is `reword`
when a criterion, clause, or invariant names that condition it is `criterion-anchored` instead

clauses.title: New blocker keys are normalized against the settled ledger
requires: normalizes the finding against the settled ledger by counterexample class
same helper or clause, same invariant, different input
reopen of the settled key requiring materially new evidence, never as a new key (CL-D34)

clauses.title: README states the anchoring bound
requires: Under CL-D34, every blocking Sol finding is anchored to an acceptance criterion, contract clause, or fail-stop invariant
`reword` finding
`follow-up` findings
bounds severity without weakening falsification

clauses.title: The six-file authority baseline is raised by owner decision
clauses.section: ## CL-D34 — Sol findings are anchored to acceptance criteria and a declared threat model
requires: raise the six-file authority baseline from 99,182 to 108,000 bytes
the byte baseline is a review guard with deliberate headroom, not a target
